title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
As the 2026–2027 school year begins, the Clay City School Board formed a committee to assess the high school’s sustainability and the district’s long-term plans. Board members Dusty Thompson and Oliver Bangert will serve on the committee and work with the Illinois State Board of Education (ISBE).  The committee was one of several topics discussed at last night’s board meeting.

Superintendent John Neubaum provided a bar graph for the last 10 years of the district’s enrollment.  The totals this year are five students less than last year.  High School enrollment has gone up but grade school enrollment is down.  Neubaum said there has been a decline in the village population and birth rates are down and parents are opting for other forms of education include private schools and home schooling.  “We have retained the high school students but the decline in elementary students will hit high school totals in the next few years,” Neubaum explained.

In the financial report the board approved Superintendent Neubaum to use $300,000 in CDs to cover bills until the tax distribution is made.  He said the bank does not charge penalties to the school district.  He also voiced concerns about the future of State transportation funding.  “Enrollment affects our funding from the State, so we have to use our funds responsibly,” Neubaum said.

He then explained the Civil Rights Compliance audit findings which was based on race, sex and disabilities.  There were three issues noted: counseling materials, non-discrimination statements, a language interpreter and one for hearing impaired students in the district.

There will be a Universal Mental Health screening conducted for students in third through 12th grade, starting with the next school year.  Neubaum said parents can opt out of this.  The superintendent also said he would be attending the IASA Conference in Springfield and the Triple I Convention in November.

The FY-27 preliminary budget was passed by the board, and they approved Carlie Travis as a full-time substitute high school science teacher.

Principal Brian Wattles provided the kindergarten through 12th grade report.  He said Gerry Brooks provided a fun and informative Teachers Institute which combined humor and passion to encourage educators and support their continued growth.  The 8th grade students will be taking a field trip as part of the Young Eagles program at Noble Airport.  Teacher Candace Walker will be the 8th grade class sponsor, and Nathan Deain was hired as the basketball coach.  Jackson Dye and Jerrin Worrell were also approved as Co-op custodians.

The board approved the price for a staff lunch at $4 with the guarantee this would include larger portions.

Following a closed session the only action was to increase the Superintendent’s salary.

title: XENIA FIRE DEPARTMENT FISH FRY
full_story:
The Xenia Fire Department Fish Fry will be held tomorrow in the Xenia Village Park.  Lunch will be served starting at 11 am.  Along with fish sandwiches there will be hot dogs, fries and drinks.  There will also be, Poe’d Smoked BBQ, Kernel Pop a flavored lemonade stand and other vendors.

The tractor pull and car show registration begin at Noon with admission $10 for adults and children 12 and under are free.  Pit passes are $15.  Car show awards will be at 3 pm.

There will be Carnival Games and prizes, inflatables and a petting zoo from Noon to 4 pm, with a $3 armband available good for unlimited activities.  There will be a silent auction at Noon.  The cake walk will be at 4 pm, bingo in the fire station starts at 5 pm and there will be live music by Molly Seaton and the Jake Perry Band from 7 to 10 pm.

The fire department is now accepting cakes, pies, and desserts for the cake walk.  Cakes can be dropped off at Fire station tonight or tomorrow morning.  Firemen are asking for non refrigerated items.

Please follow the designated event parking signs.  All proceeds from the day go to the Xenia Volunteer Fire Department.

title: NORTH WAYNE SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The North Wayne School Board tentatively approved the 2026-27 district budget and introduced new employees.

The board tentatively approved the 2026-27 budget, setting a public hearing for September 23rd at 5:50 PM at Cisne Middle School.  Todd Cyrulik from BLDD architectural firm presented future options for the district.  Board members approved a $2,500 donation to the Community Connections Fund and a $500 donation to Cisne High School FFA from Fairfield National Bank.

In personnel matters new employees Avery Smith, Ashley Shreve, Libby Pearson, Jim Farleigh, Paul Lowe, April Walker, and Chandler Courtright were introduced.  Izzy Serles was hired as an individual aide for the upcoming school year and Katlyn Tannahill’s resignation as an aide was accepted.

title: WAYNE COUNTY CROP TOUR SET
full_story:
The Wayne County Corn and Soybean Yield Tour is set for Monday.  Gregg Barnard, Corn Grower President notes this will be the 43rd year for the tour.

Last year the soybean yield was 50.3 bushels per acre on 165,500 acres and a corn yield of 164.2 bushels per acre on 102,700 acres.

As in the past, eight teams will travel different routes, each checking at least 10 soybean and 10 corn fields for yield.  The teams will leave from JT’s in Wayne City at 7 am and meet back at the Wayne City Community Building at 11:30 am to compile the yield estimates.

Anyone interested in participating in the tour should contact the Wayne County Extension Office at 618-842-3702.  The crop tour is sponsored by Wayne County Corn Growers and University of Illinois Extension.  FNB Community Bank will provide lunch for participants.

title: FCC SENIOR CITIZENS DAY
full_story:
Frontier Community College will host a Senior Citizen’s Day event on Friday, September 25th, in West Hall, rooms 103, 104 and 105.

The event is designed to provide helpful information, resources, and support for senior citizens.  The morning will feature presentations from local professionals on topics including financial estate planning, resiliency, hospital resources, healthy meals, adult education, and tutoring opportunities.

Registration and breakfast will begin at 8 am, followed by opening remarks at 8:30 am from Frontier Community College President Dr. Sharmila Kakac and Lori Noe, Director of Learning Commons.

Luke Harl, Financial Advisor with FNB Financial, will present “Financial Estate Planning for Senior Citizens” from 9 to 9:30.  Following a short break, Dana Taylor, Chief Operating Officer at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, will speak on “Resiliency Through Life Challenges” from 9:45 to 10:05.  Taylor will also share information about specialized resources and services available at Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

Additional sessions will include guided breathing imagery provided by Fairfield Memorial Hospital, “Healthy Snacks – Healthy Meals” with Whitney Buckles of Fairfield Memorial Hospital, and “Adult Education – Tutoring Opportunities” with Sharis Wilson, Director of Literacy and Adult Education Operations.

The event will conclude with door prizes and adjournment from 11:30 to noon.  A tour of Learning Commons in Cox Hall will be offered afterward.  During the tour, attendees can learn more about the accommodations and services available to senior citizens upon request.

Advance registration is required to attend.  To register, call Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711.

title: ISP ARREST PARENTS
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Division of Criminal Investigation Zone 7 Special Agents arrested 28-year-old Amanda Russell and 34-year-old Michael Russell of Du Quoin, for Involuntary Manslaughter among other charges after the death of their 1-year-old daughter.

On Monday, the Du Quoin Police Department requested ISP’s assistance with a child death investigation in the 700 block of West Park Street in Du Quoin.  The child suffered severe burns over a large portion of her body and had not been taken to a medical facility for treatment.  After a thorough investigation, ISP Special Agents arrested the parents, Amanda and Michael Russell.

On Tuesday, ISP Special Agents presented the case to the Perry County State’s Attorney’s Office and Amanda and Michael were charged with Involuntary Manslaughter a Class 2 Felony, and Endangering the Life or Health of a Child a Class 3 Felony.  Additionally, Amanda was charged with Solicitation to Obstruct Justice a Class A Misdemeanor.

title: HONOR FLIGHT 78
full_story:
Land of Lincoln Honor Flight will be taking Mission #78 on September 1st from Springfield Abraham Lincoln Capital Airport.

Mission #78 will serve 92 veterans – 5 Korean and 87 Vietnam Era Veterans – from 52 Illinois home towns.

These Veterans and their Guardians will report September 1st to the Abraham Lincoln Capitol Airport at 4:00 AM to travel to Washington DC to visit the World War II, Korean and Vietnam War Memorials, as well as Arlington National Cemetery Tomb of the Unknowns, the Lincoln Memorial, the National Air & Space Museum in Chantilly, Virginia, the US Marine Corps Memorial and the US Air Force Memorial.  This day of honor is provided at absolutely no cost to veterans and is completely funded by donations from the general public.

These 92 heroes will return to the Springfield airport at 9:30 PM on Tuesday September 1st.  The general public, friends, family and LLHF alumni veterans are encouraged to pack the airport to welcome home these heroes.  Greeters are encouraged to arrive early and show appreciation for and support of these veterans who sacrificed so much for our country.  Parking is free and volunteers will be in the parking area to assist guests to open spaces.  A shuttle bus is available to take guests from the parking lot directly to the airport terminal door.

Any veteran who served at any time up through May 7th, 1975 is eligible to participate on an Honor Flight regardless of where they served or their assigned duties.  Any seriously impaired or terminally ill WWII, Korean era or Vietnam era veteran will be given flight priority.  Veteran and Guardian Applications may be obtained at www.LandofLincolnHonorFlight.org by clicking on “Applications” tab.  LLHF also offers a “Flightless Honor Flight” program for those otherwise eligible veterans whose physical condition limits their ability to participate on an actual flight.

Land of Lincoln Honor Flight is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization.  It is only able to honor veterans due to the generous donations, sponsorships, fundraising events, merchandise sales and supporting efforts of the many local businesses, individuals, and organizations within the service area.

title: LAKE SHELBYVILLE DEER STAND AUCTION
full_story:
Friends of Lake Shelbyville, an association that works with the US Army Corps of Engineers’, is holding a silent auction for impounded deer stands and climbing sticks on Saturday, August 28th.  You’ll need to head to the government vehicle lot south of the Lake Shelbyville Visitor Center from 7:30 to 10:30 am.  Organizers say 25 tree stands will be up for bid, ranging from two-man ladder stands to single-man ladders and mobile hunting stands.

Proceeds from the auction go toward funding the Annual Youth Deer Hunt in October and the Annual Disabled Deer Hunt in November, so every bid helps support those programs.  Anyone interested can view all the stands and sticks in person that morning before deciding what to bid on.

Bidders will need to fill out a bid sheet with their contact information, the stand numbers they’re bidding on, and their bid amounts, along with a liability form releasing the Army Corps of Engineers from responsibility if an accident were to occur following your purchase.  Sealed bids will be opened at 10:30 am, and stands will be awarded to the high bidders at 11 am that same morning.  If a high bidder isn’t present at that time, the stand goes to the next highest bidder, and stands cannot be held or picked up later.

Any questions about the silent auction or Lake Shelbyville’s Tree Stand Policy can contact Park Ranger Tanner Coleman at 217-774-3951, ext. 7006, or visit the Lake Shelbyville website for more information.

title: MONITORING SPOTTED LANTERNFLY
full_story:
Monitoring continues for spotted lanternfly in Illinois.  Confirmation of the invasive pest has been limited to Cook County according to State Ag Pest Survey Coordinator Kelly Estes.

Adult spotted lanternfly are one-inch long with gray-brown forewings featuring black spots and striking bright red hindwings.  Nymphs are small and black with white spots.  You can report suspected spotted lanternfly with image to [email protected].
